The fixture is ESLint's RuleTester case `/* eslint-disable rule-to-test/max-classes-per-file */`: RuleTester registers the rule under the alias rule-to-test/max-classes-per-file, and the generator, which runs the rule under its own id max-classes-per-file, reports 3:1 because ESLint matches directive names exactly. The port also honours Oxlint 1.88.0's comments (suppress.oxlint `max-classes-per-file`), and Oxlint matches a directive name with a `/` by its part after the last `/` (crates/oxc_linter/src/disable_directives.rs at oxlint_v1.88.0), so the alias silences the port here. The disagreement is the harness's alias, not the rule: without the alias neither tool's directive would apply, and with ESLint's real id both would.

This file is the rename variant of max-classes-per-file/004.js, whose divergence is declared above, and it disagrees for the same reason: only the class names change (A, B to P, K), and the comment `/* eslint-disable rule-to-test/max-classes-per-file */` is kept. RuleTester registers the rule under the alias rule-to-test/max-classes-per-file, so ESLint, matching directive names exactly, reports 3:1 under the generator's id max-classes-per-file. The port honours Oxlint 1.88.0's comments (suppress.oxlint `max-classes-per-file`), and Oxlint matches a directive name with a `/` by its part after the last `/` (crates/oxc_linter/src/disable_directives.rs at oxlint_v1.88.0), so the alias silences the port here. The disagreement is the harness's alias, not the rule.

Line 27 is `var eval = exports.parse.eval = function(content) {` at the top level; the label 27:5 is the ESLint test set's recorded finding, which only sourceType script reproduces: there the declaration's initializer is a write reference to the global `eval` variable, which no-eval reports (ESLint 10.11.0 `new Linter().verify`, only no-eval on: 12:13 and 27:5). At its defaults (espree 11.2.0, ecmaVersion latest, sourceType module) the pinned tool cannot parse the file (fatal `Binding eval in strict mode` at 27:5, no no-eval finding), and under sourceType commonjs it reports only 12:13. Rerail reads the file as Node does (no package.json type, no module syntax: CommonJS), where the top-level `var eval` is module-local and the port reports 12:13 as ESLint does; under a script unit language it reports 27:5 too (clause eval-declaration-write). The two cannot be compared on this line without the sourceType the test set chose. Remove when samples carry the sourceType they were labelled under.
